# Parallel-sync policy: independent code quality runtime addendum

Verdict: **PASS** for the pure Rust capability-policy source and its owner runtime gates. No blocking quality finding.

Reviewed source commit `63c88dcf0eb7364521c5ea79b8cd67e63e4990b0`, tree `cc64dc5e95b8998ef8392135cbc54cea27776a59`, in `/workspace/android-studio-parallel-sync-policy`. This addendum supplements the unchanged static quality review, SHA-256 `d707659b72b6902c52014def7df9f4149468243a8ff6204c8e01ab37aa9e072e`. It does not supersede that report or its preserved correction history.

## Source and conventions

I reread the repository `.rules`, `docs/AGENTS.md`, the prior static quality review, the current policy module and tests, the retained Apache originals and NOTICE, the owner plan and mapping, the execution recipe, and the actual raw logs and structured receipts. The additive descriptive module and export follow the existing Zed crate layout. There is no new crate, dependency, lockfile change, scheduler, UI callback, background task, global state, filesystem operation, unsafe code or non-Rust component in this six-file diff.

Production parsing uses borrowed string splits and fixed scalar fields, propagates existing typed failures, and introduces no unwrap, expect, unchecked indexing or silently discarded fallible result. Derived ordering follows the pinned numeric/kind/preview field order and `Alpha < Beta < Rc < Dev < Stable`. Tuple comparison of producer versions preserves signed extrema without subtraction. The 64-byte input bound admits every valid pinned spelling, whose maximum length is 40 bytes, while bounding scan work and diagnostic size. Historical preview padding, leading-zero rejection, ASCII grammar and signed-Int bounds agree with the retained parser. Invalid explicit AGP facts are validated before a newer producer can enable the feature. An unavailable minimum-consumer value remains irrelevant to this specific predicate.

The two private AGP parsers remain a documented maintenance advisory, as in the static report. Extracting a shared parser would alter the frozen inherited V2 contract and broaden this prerequisite. No such refactor is required for this PASS.

Its optional local extra-tool chain stops when `cargo-shear` is unavailable; the required strict Clippy command completed successfully. No unavailable optional tool is credited as having run.

Other shared-cache artifact hashes are identities at execution time; subsequent authorized Root builds may replace those cache paths. Their continued existence is not used as a current quality gate.

## Reference coverage and preservation

The Rust original-method test retains all nine positive/negative AGP literals in their original order, the original signed `Int.MIN_VALUE` producer tuple, empty description, and both named-message meanings. The retained `ModelVersionsTest.kt` bytes and complete original method were compared directly. The original null unused minimum consumer is represented by an explicitly unavailable unused captured field, as documented in the helper and Apache NOTICE. This adds no requirement absent from the reference and removes no assertion.

Nine additional declared tests cover the preview/micro endpoints, all 100 valid 7.3 alpha spellings, signed producer override and description preservation, typed missing/not-applicable input, malformed and unknown-qualifier precedence even with a newer producer, historical spelling, numeric bounds, and long-input diagnostic bounds. All ten policy tests appear in the unfiltered passing group. No ignore, should-panic, deleted assertion or weakened test was introduced by this policy task.

I independently rehashed all **4,717** fixed-scope source bindings against the static guard and runtime snapshot, all **148** rebounded immutable originals, all six policy blobs, all three reference identities, and all four explicitly approved inherited Root-correction blobs. Every hash matches. All ten before/after runtime snapshots are identical; the current index and Git status also match those snapshots. The seven source pathspecs are unchanged and still guard code, fixtures, assets and nested `docs/android-studio/ports/evidence/` content. No exclusion was widened.

The three freshness receipts each touch only the eight crate/test roots, retain matching content hashes, and record increasing mtimes. The recipe verifies the source/index/status snapshot before and after those byte-identical freshness changes. This appropriately prevents cross-worktree falsely fresh Cargo results without changing source bytes or compiler flags.

Complete Apache-attributed originals, license and precise NOTICE remain intact. Historical static/proposal files accurately record their earlier execution-pending state; the new actual-check receipts supply current runtime evidence. No complete upstream suite census or canonical parity promotion is inferred from the one owner exact execution. Its structured receipt correctly retains `canonical_parity_credit: 0` and lead capture pending.

## Scope and pending lead gates

This PASS establishes code quality and actual owner execution for the Rust eligibility policy. It does not claim actual parallel Gradle scheduling, UI wiring, full-app behavior, full-workspace CI, canonical lead reference capture, protected-branch merge, Phase 1 completion or completion of the IDE. The matching-source full-app/native/full-CI and canonical lead gates remain Root responsibilities before merge.

This review performed source/reference/log/hash reads and wrote only this external addendum. It ran no Cargo, rustc, Clippy, formatter, test, Gradle or native app process; changed no source, cache, original report or Git state; and dispatched no subagents. Root's exclusive execution lease remains undisturbed.
